pages.title: Muhanad Abdelrahim — Agentic Founder · Product Strategist
pages.description: Muhanad Abdelrahim builds Steller, a live B2B gift card platform, with AI agents and no engineering team. Based in Mississauga, Ontario.

pages.title: Essays & field notes — Muhanad Abdelrahim
pages.description: Essays and field notes from building Steller: agentic architecture, product-led onboarding, and the complete founder story.

pages.title: Built From the Rubble — The Steller Story
pages.description: A development team displaced by war, a codebase full of invisible debt, and 27 days to fix Steller before the first partner integration deadline.

pages.title: We Stopped Teaching. We Started Doing. — Steller PLG 2.0
pages.description: PLG used to mean reducing friction. The real unlock is removing the work entirely — how we applied that to Steller onboarding.

pages.title: Steller: The Complete Story — What actually happened
pages.description: The earlier essay got the facts right and the story wrong. The rebuild was a redesign, the onboarding was a philosophy, and this is the complete account.

pages.title: What Belongs in AGENTS.md
pages.description: What Steller’s AGENTS.md files actually contain: a short router, backend locks, and the commands that close a session.

pages.title: The Agent Handover Protocol
pages.description: The hardening week named four protocol files. One can be quoted. Three cannot, and this essay does not invent them.

pages.title: What Zero Full-Time Developers Actually Requires
pages.description: Zero full-time developers is Steller’s published operating claim. It depends on a visible flow, locks, and a human approval on production.

pages.title: When Fat Controllers Stop Working
pages.description: Fat controllers fixed a context-window failure. The same essay already states the three conditions where they stop.

pages.title: Why Explicit Jobs Beat Invisible Events for AI
pages.description: RabbitMQ hid the next file. PlaceBambooOrderJob is a named job with a no-retry and refund lock.

pages.title: The Failure-First Onboarding
pages.description: Invalid key, empty catalog, unfunded wallet — the three failures both onboarding essays surface, in each essay’s own step order.

pages.title: 202 Accepted Is a Product Decision
pages.description: 202 is the value signal, not the PIN. The essays and the developer hub do not publish the same poll interval.

pages.title: Idempotency for Gift Card APIs
pages.description: referenceId is the partner replay field. Bamboo’s Idempotency-Key is a separate operator lock.

pages.title: Doing the Customer’s Work Before They Ask
pages.description: The published path from Sudan business development to Steller’s 60-second onboarding, without unpublished deals.

pages.title: The Economics of Agent-Operated Software
pages.description: The published pivot cost is $672 over 27 days. The weekly buckets are not a second invoice, and zero developers is not free.
